headline: Quiet day, just one security heads-up
summary: No big launches; Convex's skills are reported to quietly send your app ideas to a remote server

items.title: Convex skills reportedly leak your ideas
items.what: Convex is a platform that handles the backend for apps (storing data, running server logic). It put out skills for AI coding assistants (a skill is a bundle of instructions plus scripts that teaches an AI how to do something). The HN post title says these skills send your app ideas to a remote server without telling you. I couldn't find the original post, so I don't know what exactly gets sent or whether it's on by default.
items.meaning: Treat it as a heads-up: before installing any third-party skill, check whether it phones home. It doesn't affect you much unless you use Convex.
deep_dive: What I could confirm from searching: Convex's convex-quickstart can scaffold an app from a one-line idea. There's also a plugin that sends your session transcript to the Convex team for review, and that's stated openly in its description. I can't confirm whether this is the same thing as the post.

General advice: before installing any skill for Claude Code or codex, open its SKILL.md and any bundled scripts and look for network calls or uploads. You can also ask an AI to read it through for you.
